minutes.headline: Commissioners cut a resident's exorbitant leak-driven water bill to tier-one rate and vowed to fix failed notifications
minutes.summary: The Water District Commissioners heard two residents' high-usage/leak bills, voted to move the 386 Hollis Road account to the lowest rate tier with an interest-free payment plan, and acknowledged the district's notice letter never reached the customer. The board also approved a one-year subscription to Waterworth Utility Management for long-term financial and rate modeling, left the board's current organization in place, and discussed an unresolved problem of fire department hydrant use causing water main pressure spikes and a broken main, with training to be arranged with the fire chief.

what_happened.line: Commissioners voted to drop a leak-driven high-usage bill to the lowest rate tier and allow an interest-free payment plan.
The board acknowledged its notice letter about the high reading never reached the resident before the bill arrived.
Commissioners voted to enter a one-year subscription with Waterworth Utility Management for rate and capital planning.
Going forward, staff will follow up daily on an unanswered customer notice instead of leaving it unresolved.
The board discussed fire department hydrant use triggering water-main pressure spikes and a broken main, with training to be scheduled with the fire chief.

why_it_matters: A resident's water bill was reduced by board vote after a leak, which touches how the district treats other high-usage or leak-driven bills going forward.
The failed notification prompted a new daily-follow-up policy, which affects how quickly any customer learns of an unusual reading before a bill arrives.
A paid modeling subscription and unresolved hydrant-pressure problem both bear on future water rates and infrastructure costs.
